title: Plaza governed-document frontmatter
description: The technical contract every governed document in the 10110 TastesLike Plaza doc set carries in its YAML frontmatter. Authority is declared here, in machine-readable form, so 'which document wins' is a lookup rather than an argument. Governed by specs/meta/META-SPEC.md; enforced by scripts/validate_specs.py.

doc_id.description: Stable identifier. Never changes when the file moves; cross-references cite this, not the path.

title.description: Human-readable name. Should match the document's H1.

tier.description: Position in the hierarchy. Lower wins. 0 = meta layer (governs the doc set itself), 1 = concept source of truth, 2 = implementation + canonical reference, 3 = derived plans, 4 = derived summaries and non-authoritative inputs.

authority.description: What this document is allowed to decide. See META-SPEC section 2.

x-may-originate.$comment: Which authorities may appear on a document that declares `decides`. The four omitted values (derived, summary, research, historical) are licensed to originate nothing, so a `decides` list on one of them is a contradiction; scripts/validate_specs.py reads this list and fails the build. This is the COARSE gate only -- it says an authority may originate something, not that a given decision falls within that authority's subject matter. Whether a constitution document is deciding about documents (permitted) or about the product (not) is a judgement no validator makes. `delivery` (D-028) joined in v0.2.10: time-boxed operational policy that expires with its artifact, licensed at tier 3.

doc_set_version.description: Semantic version of the doc SET this file is aligned to. The set carries one version; individual files do not version independently.

last_updated.description: Month the file was last substantively edited, as YYYY-MM.

owner.description: GitHub handle accountable for the document's content.

derives_from.description: doc_ids this document derives decisions from. A document may never contradict anything it derives from.

supersedes.description: doc_ids this document replaces as an authority.

decides.description: Decision IDs (D-nnn) this document is the origin of. The rule is the authority, not the tier: a document may claim these only when its `authority` appears in authority.x-may-originate. That was tier 0-2 in every release up to v0.2.9, and the old wording said so; D-028 added tier-3 `delivery`, so the tier shorthand is no longer equivalent to the rule and has been dropped rather than extended. Registered in specs/meta/decision-register.md.

enforcement.$comment: OPTIONAL IN v0.2.10, BY DESIGN, AND ONLY UNTIL THE SET IS MIGRATED. The enum below binds whenever the key is present, so a wrong value fails today; a MISSING value does not, because you cannot switch on a required field before populating it -- T6 (PLZG-136) assigns all 24 documents, and only then does T3 (PLZG-134) make absence fail. If you are reading this after PLZG-136 landed and absence still passes, that is the bug.
enforcement.description: How far this document's claims about state are actually proven. Per document, valued at its WEAKEST state claim. See META-SPEC section 2.1 (D-027). `enforced` = a named CI gate re-derives every state claim on every run. `asserted` = a human verified it at a stated date, nothing re-checks. `intended` = aspiration, explicitly not yet true. `n/a` = the document makes no claims about state, which is off the scale rather than its bottom rung. Governs claims about the repository, the board, the running system and the tooling -- NOT decisions, which are governed by `authority`. An `intended` value restricts nothing about originating decisions.

gates.$comment: ENCODED AS `job:type` STRINGS, NOT AS {job, type} OBJECTS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS FORCED. parse_frontmatter() in scripts/validate_specs.py supports `key: scalar` and `key: [a, b]` only -- a deliberately narrow YAML subset, so the contract stays readable without a YAML library. A nested block list errors loudly ('nested frontmatter is not supported'), which is survivable; the inline form `[{job: X, type: live}]` SILENTLY MISPARSES to ['{job: X', 'type: live}'], which is not. The pattern below rejects both, so the dangerous shape fails the build rather than validating as nonsense. sprint-3-charter.md section 4 check 2 and sprint-3-loop-plan.md's T2 note both originally said {job, type} objects; both were PATCHED in PLZG-133 under META-SPEC section 4 rule 1, which is the branch of the conflict protocol that applies when one side is unambiguously higher tier on the relevant axis -- tier 0 owns how frontmatter is encoded. Not recorded in the open-conflict register, because that is rule 2, for conflicts where the tier is ambiguous. The job name and the type are both still carried and both still checked; only the encoding changed.
gates.description: CI gates backing this document's state claims, each as `<job name>:<type>` -- for example `Validate Specs:live`. Type `live` means the gate re-derives the fact from the system that owns it; `snapshot` means it reads committed data. ENFORCED TODAY (v0.2.10), by the pattern below: the `job:type` shape and the type vocabulary. NOT YET ENFORCED, PENDING T3/PLZG-134: that the job name exists in .github/workflows/ci.yml; that `enforced`/`asserted` declare a NON-EMPTY list; and that `enforced` carries at least one `live` entry (D-027, rule 4). Those three are cross-field and cross-file rules that this schema subset cannot express -- a `minItems` the validator silently ignores would read as coverage it does not have -- so they land in scripts/validate_specs.py, not here. Stated in two tenses deliberately: a contract that describes a pending check in the present tense is the exact defect the enforcement axis exists to surface.

weakest_claim.$comment: The falsifiability hook, and the reason this axis is not self-certification. A reviewer checks the quote against the document in ten seconds, and a fabricated audit fails the build. KNOWN LIMIT, STATED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED AS A DEFECT: the validator proves the quote is REAL, never that it is the WEAKEST -- a document may cite a trivially true sentence and still pass. That is the third instance of the same class (authority cannot check subject matter, constitution cannot check whether a decision is product-shaped), and review is still the check. Accepted cost: this duplicates prose into frontmatter, so editing that sentence breaks the build until this is updated -- chosen knowingly, since editing your weakest claim is exactly when the value should be re-examined.
weakest_claim.description: For `asserted` and `intended` documents: the single weakest state claim the document makes, quoted so it appears VERBATIM in the document body. ENFORCED TODAY (v0.2.10): the type and a minimum length. NOT YET ENFORCED, PENDING T3/PLZG-134: the substring match against the document body, which is what actually makes the value falsifiable. Until T3 lands, a `weakest_claim` naming no real sentence will pass -- said plainly rather than implied, because this field's whole purpose is to stop a document claiming more proof than it has.
